condition: Screening in an 81-year-old man — avoid over-screening
permutationLabel: Age 81, fit, normal colonoscopy at 71; asks for PSA and bowel test
summary: 81-year-old fit man, normal colonoscopy at 71, asks for a "full check-up with the prostate test and a bowel test". USPSTF: recommend against PSA screening ≥ 70 (D); CRC screening 76–85 is selective (C), guided by health and prior screening; no AAA screening after 75.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Wants a full check-up including the prostate test and a bowel test
inputs.hpi: Fit 81-year-old retired farmer, walks 3 miles daily. Asks for "the prostate blood test" and "a bowel test" because a friend was diagnosed. No urinary symptoms, no bowel symptoms, no weight loss. Colonoscopy at 71 was normal. Never smoked.

exam.abdomen: Soft, no masses; no palpable aorta.

inputs.socialHistory: Retired farmer, never smoked, lives with wife.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Health check, age 81 — screening review
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic 81-year-old. PSA screening not recommended at this age (discussed). Colorectal screening at 76–85 is an individual decision; normal colonoscopy at 71, good health — discussed options.

mustExclude.note: USPSTF 2018 grade D: recommend against PSA-based screening in men ≥ 70.

mustInclude.note: At 76–85 CRC screening is selective (grade C): the plan should mention individual health, life expectancy and prior screening.

mustExclude.note: A PSA screening discussion "for men ≥ 50" at 81 contradicts USPSTF grade D.
Routine 10-yearly colonoscopy is not the default above 75.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for prostate cancer
guideline.section: 55–69: individual decision about PSA-based screening after discussion of potential benefits and harms (grade C); ≥ 70: recommend against PSA-based screening (grade D); Black men and men with a family history may benefit from the discussion
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for prostate cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2018;319:1901–1913.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Screen adults 45–49 (grade B) and 50–75 (grade A); 76–85 selectively, considering overall health and prior screening (grade C); stool-based (e.g. annual FIT) or direct visualisation (e.g. colonoscopy every 10 years) strategies
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for colorectal cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325:1965–1977.

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm
guideline.section: Men 65–75 who have ever smoked: one-time ultrasound screening for AAA (grade B)
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2019;322:2211–2218.

rationale: Screening beyond the evidence-based age range causes harm (overdiagnosis, colonoscopy complications). USPSTF: no PSA screening at ≥ 70; CRC screening 76–85 only selectively; AAA screening is for men 65–75 who have ever smoked.
